Series::logical_not¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::logical_not() const -> Series

What It Does¶

logical_not() flips truth values lane by lane and returns the result as a boolean Series.

The public rule is simple:

  • zero-like or false-like lanes become true

  • non-zero or true-like lanes become false

Numeric inputs are first interpreted by truthiness:

  • 0 becomes false

  • any non-zero numeric value becomes true

The in-place sibling logical_not_() follows the same truthiness rule and simply stores the result back into self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series containing the truth-value inverse of self.

Examples¶

Example 1. Numeric inputs are converted to truthiness first, then inverted.

auto values = pluss::make_series({0, 2, 0, -5}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);

pluss::series::print(std::cout, values.logical_not());

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true, false]

The interpretation is:

  • 0 is false, so !0 becomes true

  • 2 is true, so !2 becomes false

  • -5 is also true, so it becomes false

Example 2. Boolean input follows the same rule without a numeric conversion step.

auto mask = pluss::make_series({true, false, true, false},
                               pluss::ScalarType::Bool);
std::cout << mask.logical_not();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[false, true, false, true]

Example 3. The out-of-place method preserves the original Series.

auto values = pluss::make_series({0.0, 2.0, 0.0, -5.0});
auto inverted = values.logical_not();
std::cout << values << "\n";
std::cout << inverted;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 2, 0, -5]
pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, true, false]

Gradient¶

Logical negation is a boolean mask transform. It does not define a numeric derivative through the zero-versus-non-zero decision.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The result dtype is boolean.

  • Numeric truthiness is based on zero vs non-zero, not on exact equality to 1.

  • Because the result is boolean, integer or floating-point inputs do not keep their original dtype on the returned Series.

Summary¶

Use logical_not() when you need a boolean inverse mask while preserving the original Series.

See Also¶

  • Series::logical_not_: same truth-value inversion, but written back into self.

  • Series::logical_and: combine masks by conjunction.

  • Series::bitwise_not: raw bit inversion instead of truth-value inversion.
